# Lead

The paragraph under a page title that says what the screen is for, in the reading voice.

Status: Stable. Semantic versioning applies: nothing breaks without a deprecation first.

The one place a tool speaks in prose: the paragraph under a page title that explains what this screen is for. Alegreya — the reading voice — because it is read once, properly, not scanned.

## Usage

### When to use

- One or two sentences under a page or section title, read once on a first visit.
- The explanation under a Display title on an onboarding or first-run screen.

### When not to

- Interface text, such as descriptions and hints. Use [Text](https://demogar.github.io/molaui/md/components-typography-text--overview.md).
- Several paragraphs of long-form content. Use [Prose](https://demogar.github.io/molaui/md/components-typography-prose--overview.md).

### Content

- Say what the screen is for and what the reader can do there, in plain sentences.

## Examples

Each story is a live example in Storybook.

- [Default](https://demogar.github.io/molaui/?path=/story/components-typography-lead--default)

## API

### `Lead` (component)

The first thing someone says, so it is set in the reading voice rather than the system one. Alegreya from here down; Archivo above and around.

`className`, `ref`, `id` and the other DOM props go to `<p data-slot="lead">`.

## Accessibility

Nothing in it takes focus, so there is no keyboard table.

### Mola handles

- Renders a `<p>` held to the reading measure.

### You handle

- Use it once, under the page title; it is not a heading.
